The '''shifted log-logistic distribution''' is a [[probability distribution]] also known as the '''generalized log-logistic''' or the '''three-parameter log-logistic''' distribution.<ref>
{{Citation|first=Gary G.|last=Venter| pages=91–101| title=Introduction to selected papers from the variability in reserves prize program | journal=Casualty Actuarial Society Forum |  date=Spring 1994| volume=1| url=http://www.casact.org/pubs/forum/94spforum/94spf091.pdf}}</ref><ref>
{{Citation| first=Ronald B. |last=Geskus |title=Methods for estimating the AIDS incubation time distribution when date of seroconversion is censored| journal=Statistics in Medicine| volume=20| pages=795–812| year=2001| doi=10.1002/sim.700| issue=5| pmid=11241577}}</ref> It has also been called the '''generalized logistic''' distribution,<ref name=Hosking97>{{Citation|title=Regional Frequency Analysis: An Approach Based on L-Moments| first1=Jonathan R. M. | last1=Hosking|
first2= James R| last2=Wallis| year=1997| publisher=Cambridge University Press| isbn=0-521-43045-3}}</ref> but this conflicts with other uses of the term: see [[generalized logistic distribution]].

==Definition==
The shifted log-logistic distribution can be obtained from the [[log-logistic distribution]] by addition of a [[Location parameter|shift parameter]] <math>\delta</math>. Thus if <math>X</math> has a log-logistic distribution then <math>X+\delta</math> has a shifted log-logistic distribution. So  <math>Y</math> has a shifted log-logistic distribution if <math>\log(Y-\delta)</math> has a logistic distribution. The shift parameter adds a location parameter to the  scale and shape parameters of the (unshifted) log-logistic.

The properties of this distribution are straightforward to derive from those of the log-logistic distribution. However, an alternative parameterisation, similar to that used for the [[Pareto distribution#Generalized Pareto distributions|generalized Pareto distribution]] and the [[generalized extreme value distribution]], gives more interpretable parameters and also aids their estimation.

In this parameterisation, the [[cumulative distribution function]] (CDF) of the shifted log-logistic distribution is
: <math>F(x; \mu,\sigma,\xi) = \frac{1}{ 1 + \left(1+ \frac{\xi(x-\mu)}{\sigma}\right)^{-1/\xi}}</math>
for <math> 1 + \xi(x-\mu)/\sigma \geqslant 0</math>, where <math>\mu\in\mathbb R</math> is the location parameter, <math>\sigma>0\,</math> the scale parameter and <math>\xi\in\mathbb R</math> the shape parameter.  Note that some references use <math> \kappa =  - \xi\,\!</math> to parameterise the shape.<ref name=Hosking97/><ref name=FEH/>

The [[probability density function]] (PDF) is 
:<math> f(x; \mu,\sigma,\xi) = \frac{\left(1+\frac{\xi(x-\mu)}{\sigma}\right)^{-(1/\xi +1)}}
{\sigma\left[1 + \left(1+\frac{\xi(x-\mu)}{\sigma}\right)^{-1/\xi}\right]^2}, </math>
again, for <math> 1 + \xi(x-\mu)/\sigma \geqslant 0. </math>

The shape parameter <math>\xi</math> is often restricted to lie in [-1,1], when the probability density function is bounded. When <math>|\xi|>1</math>, it has an [[asymptote]] at <math>x = \mu - \sigma/\xi</math>. Reversing the sign of <math>\xi</math> reflects the pdf and the cdf about <math>x=\mu.</math>.

===Related distributions===

* When <math>\mu = \sigma/\xi,</math> the shifted log-logistic reduces to the log-logistic distribution.
* When <math>\xi</math> → 0, the shifted log-logistic reduces to the [[logistic distribution]].
* The shifted log-logistic with shape parameter <math>\xi=1</math> is the same as the [[generalized Pareto distribution]] with shape parameter <math>\xi=1.</math>

===Applications===

The three-parameter log-logistic distribution is used in [[hydrology]] for modelling  flood frequency.<ref name=Hosking97/><ref name=FEH>
{{Citation|title=Flood Estimation Handbook | volume=3: "Statistical Procedures for Flood Frequency Estimation"| last1=Robson| first1=A. |last2=Reed| first2=D.| year=1999 |place=Wallingford, UK| publisher= Institute of Hydrology| isbn=0-948540-89-3}}</ref><ref>
{{Citation| journal=Journal of Hydrology |volume=98| year=1988 |pages=205–224| title=Log-logistic flood frequency analysis |first1=M. I. |last1=Ahmad| first2=C. D. |last2=Sinclair |first3=A. |last3=Werritty| doi=10.1016/0022-1694(88)90015-7| issue=3–4|bibcode=1988JHyd...98..205A }}</ref>

=== Alternate parameterization===
An alternate parameterization with simpler expressions for the PDF and CDF is as follows. For the shape parameter <math>\alpha</math>, scale parameter <math>\beta</math> and location parameter <math>\gamma</math>, the PDF is given by <ref name= EF>{{cite web |url=http://www.mathwave.com/help/easyfit/html/analyses/distributions/log-logistic.html |title=EasyFit - Log-Logistic Distribution |access-date=1 October 2016}}</ref><ref name= RIS>{{cite web |url=http://www.palisade.com/downloads/documentation/75/EN/RISK7_EN.pdf |title=Guide to Using - RISK7_EN.pdf |access-date=1 October 2016}}</ref> 

<math>f(x) = \frac{\alpha}{\beta} \bigg(\frac{x-\gamma}{\beta} \bigg) ^{\alpha -1}\bigg(1+\bigg(\frac{x-\gamma}{\beta}\bigg)^\alpha\bigg)^{-2}</math>

The CDF is given by 

<math>F(x) = \bigg(1+\bigg(\frac{\beta}{x-\gamma}\bigg)^\alpha\bigg)^{-1}</math>

The mean is <math>\beta \theta \csc(\theta) + \gamma</math> and the variance is <math>\beta^2\theta[2\csc(2\theta)-\theta \csc^2(\theta)]</math>, where <math>\theta = \frac{\pi}{\alpha}</math>.<ref name= RIS/>
